title: the cursor-agent auth probe checks the crew key with --list-models, which reads it, instead of status, which ignores it, and says which of no key, rejected key or keychain-only login is the problem
acceptance:
Why. Since T-188 the cursor-agent probe reports the stored crew key as `unauthenticated` ('cursor-agent says the login a round would get is not signed in; replace the crew Cursor API key …'), and fm-worker/fm-review print that line, although the crew key works. Firstmate recorded on 2026-10-05, cursor-agent 2026.10.01-e373342, macOS Darwin 24.6.0, outside any round, with `env -i HOME=<empty temp dir> TMPDIR=<temp> PATH USER`, under `sandbox-exec -p "$(python3 bin/lib/fm_sandbox_policy.py auth-probe-profile)"`:
- `cursor-agent status` prints `Not logged in` and exits 0 in all three cases: no CURSOR_API_KEY, CURSOR_API_KEY set to a placeholder (`key_bogus000000`), and CURSOR_API_KEY set to the real `firstmate-cursor-api-key` item. `status` reports only cursor's own keychain session and ignores CURSOR_API_KEY, so it cannot check the crew key at all. Run by the operator with their real HOME it prints `✓ Logged in as <email>`; that is the operator's `agent login`, which is what the 2026-09-29 'signed-in' fixture recorded, and why design.md §13.3's 'So `cursor-agent status` does read `CURSOR_API_KEY`' is wrong.
- `cursor-agent --list-models` does read the key: no key exits 1 with `Error: Authentication required. …`; the placeholder exits 1 with `Warning: The provided API key is invalid.`; the real key exits 0 and prints `Available models` and the list, after a keychain-save warning.
So the probe's check (bin/fm-auth-probe.sh:133, `argv=(cursor-agent status)`) is the wrong command, not just the wrong message. Fixing it turns a false `unauthenticated` into `authenticated` for a working key; `fm_auth_refuses` (bin/adapters/_lib.sh:311) and the rule that only `authenticated` is usable are unchanged. Whether a cursor round then succeeds is the adapter's business and out of scope. The captain asked for the misleading message to be fixed (2026-10-05).

Mechanism (cursor-agent only; claude, codex and gemini probes, argv and ordering are unchanged).
- bin/fm-auth-probe.sh:133 becomes `cursor-agent) argv=(cursor-agent --list-models) ;;`. Everything T-188 built stays: the Darwin `sandbox-exec` auth-probe profile, the `started` marker, the emptied environment, HOME `$work/tmp/home`, the timeout, never running unconfined, never printing vendor output or a secret. The same precedent: bin/adapters/cursor-agent.sh:95-101 already asks `cursor-agent --list-models`.
- Classification for cursor-agent, in this order: timeout; not started (keychain-blocked, 'could not confine …', as today); quota signatures; expiry signatures; exit 0 and a line exactly `Available models` -> `authenticated` (this wins over the keychain-save warning the real output carries); output containing `The provided API key is invalid` -> `unauthenticated` with the key-rejected reason below; a case-insensitive `keychain` with a nonzero exit -> `keychain-blocked` (the existing reasons); the `_FM_UNAUTH` signatures -> `unauthenticated` with the no-key-received reason below; anything else, including exit 0 without `Available models` -> `indeterminate`. The old `Logged in` rule for cursor is removed.
- Reasons, each in en and Traditional Chinese, printed only through `print_result` (they reach the board through FM_AUTH_EN/FM_AUTH_TW and `vendor_unavailable` events, bin/adapters/_lib.sh:274-290, unchanged):
  1. No crew key stored. login-env exit 77 alone does not mean that: it also covers an item or file that exists but cannot be read, is empty, is readable by others, or a store that could not be reached (bin/lib/fm_sandbox_policy.py:431-445, 490-496). Only the all-sources-missing form gets this reason: the `why` that `login_tier` builds as `'no ' + ' and no '.join(tried)` plus the hint (bin/lib/fm_sandbox_policy.py:493-495). The probe recognises it by `why` starting with `no ` (on macOS `no keychain item 'firstmate-cursor-api-key' and no /abs/…/cursor-api-key`; on Linux `no /abs/…/cursor-api-key`, the path being the policy's resolved absolute path, bin/lib/fm_registry.py:415-426, never the literal `~`). Every refusal form that is not absence starts otherwise (a source name, `keychain item '…' could not be read`, `<path> can be read by others…`, `<path> is empty`, or an unreached-store line), so this test is exact; every other exit-77 `why` keeps today's reason 'cursor-agent has no login a round could use: <why>' unchanged, so its actionable cause (chmod 600, could not be read (exit 36), is empty, no other source answered) is still printed. Before cursor is asked: 'no crew Cursor API key is stored; cursor-agent's own sign-in (agent login) lives in the macOS keychain, which crew rounds cannot read' followed by the existing policy hint. zh-TW: '尚未保存 crew 的 Cursor API key；cursor-agent 自己的登入（agent login）存在 macOS 鑰匙圈，crew 回合無法讀取' plus the hint. This is the 'keychain login only' case; the probe never asks the keychain whether the operator is signed in.
  2. Key stored but rejected: 'cursor rejected the crew Cursor API key as invalid; replace it: security add-generic-password -U -s firstmate-cursor-api-key -a "$USER" -w'. zh-TW: 'cursor 判定 crew 的 Cursor API key 無效；請更換：security add-generic-password -U -s firstmate-cursor-api-key -a "$USER" -w'. `-U` is required because the item already exists; without it `security` refuses to replace it.
  3. Key stored but cursor reports no credential (`Authentication required`): 'cursor-agent did not receive the crew Cursor API key; run fm doctor'. zh-TW: 'cursor-agent 沒有收到 crew 的 Cursor API key；請執行 fm doctor'.
  The cursor `fix_en`/`fix_tw` line that told the operator to replace a key that works (bin/fm-auth-probe.sh:327-329) is replaced by these per-case reasons. `authenticated` reads 'cursor-agent's model list confirms the crew Cursor API key' / 'cursor-agent 的模型清單確認 crew 的 Cursor API key 有效'.

Recorded fixtures (memory rule: stubs answer like the vendor). In tests/fixtures/auth-status, `cursor-agent-signed-in.txt` and `cursor-agent-signed-out.txt` are replaced, and `cursor-agent-key-rejected.txt` is added, each with the header keys `recorded: yes`, `command: cursor-agent --list-models`, `cli: 2026.10.01-e373342`, `date: 2026-10-05`, `host: macOS, Darwin 24.6.0, outside any round, env -i with an empty temp HOME, under the auth-probe sandbox profile`, a `setup:` line, `redacted:` and `exit:`. Bodies, verbatim (ESC is byte 0x1b, ⚠ is U+26A0; the first line's ANSI codes are kept):
- signed-in (setup: the crew key as CURSOR_API_KEY; redacted: the model list after its first two entries; exit 0):
`ESC[33m⚠ Cursor couldn't save your credentials. This session continues with the credentials it already has.ESC[0m` / `Error: Cursor couldn't save your login to the macOS keychain.` / `The keychain item is stuck. Delete it and sign in again:` / `  security delete-generic-password -s cursor-access-token -a cursor-user` / `  agent login` / `Available models` / `` / `auto - Auto (default)` / `gpt-5.3-codex-low - Codex 5.3 Low`.
- signed-out (setup: no CURSOR_API_KEY; redacted: nothing; exit 1): `Error: Authentication required. Run 'agent login', pass --api-key/--auth-token, or set CURSOR_API_KEY/CURSOR_AUTH_TOKEN.`
- key-rejected (setup: CURSOR_API_KEY=key_bogus000000; redacted: nothing; exit 1): `ESC[33m⚠ Warning: The provided API key is invalid.ESC[0m` / `The API key was loaded from the CURSOR_API_KEY environment variable.` / `Please check you have the right key, create a new one, or authenticate without it.`
The fixture loop at tests/auth-probe.test.sh:84 lists the new file, and the version assertion at tests/auth-probe.test.sh:123 becomes `2026.10.01-e373342` (with its message naming the new recording). bin/fm-doctor.sh `vendor_min` (:314-320) raises cursor-agent to 2026.10.01, the version its recording now comes from; tests/doctor.test.sh:192-196 keeps the floor equal to the fixture, and its comment block (bin/fm-doctor.sh:307-313) names the new date.

Tests (tests/** only; workers do not run suites, CI and gates verify):
- tests/auth-probe.test.sh: every cursor-agent fake answers only `--version` and `--list-models` and exits 64 on any other argv (so a probe still calling `status` fails). `fake_checks cursor-agent` (:153-162) replays signed-in when handed the crew key, else key-rejected. The stale-notes case (:164-175) keeps counting calls. Replace the invented replies at :193-205 (`✓ Logged in`, `keychain warning: not authenticated`) with the recordings: signed-in is `authenticated` despite its keychain lines; key-rejected is `unauthenticated` with reason 2 in both languages; signed-out with a key present is `unauthenticated` with reason 3; a stored-key-free run gives reason 1 without cursor being started; exit 0 without `Available models` is `indeterminate`; `Available models` with a nonzero exit is not `authenticated`; quota and expiry still win over `Available models`; a keychain error with nonzero exit is still `keychain-blocked`. Assert no vendor output line and no key reaches the probe's stdout. The T-188 confinement, profile, marker and timeout cases are kept, renamed from 'cursor status' to 'cursor check'.
- Exit-77 cases in tests/auth-probe.test.sh: with every crew source missing (`no_logins`) the reason is reason 1 in both languages, on darwin (`FM_SANDBOX_OS=darwin`, keychain item and file both missing) and on linux (file missing only, why `no /<abs path>…`); with the crew key file mode 644 (Linux tier) the reason still names `chmod 600`; with a keychain item that will not open (a fake `security` exiting 36, as tests/sandbox-login.test.sh:578-591 does) the reason still names `could not be read (exit 36`; neither of the last two is reason 1, and in none is cursor started.
- tests/lib/herdr.py:45-52: the cursor-agent `STATUS_PRELUDE` intercepts `['--list-models']` instead of `['status']`, replaying `cursor-agent-signed-out` (now the recorded `Authentication required`, exit 1); tests/herdr/credentials.py:86-113 keeps expecting cursor-agent `unauthenticated`, and its comment (:86-90, 'cursor-agent's recorded answer is "Not logged in"') names the new recording.
- tests/worker-auth.test.sh:47-55: the fake answers `--list-models` with the signed-in recording when given the key (exit 64 otherwise), and `cursor-calls` records `--list-models`.
- Fail-first: on base, the signed-in-recording case and the worker-auth case are red (base asks `status`, which the fakes refuse).

Callers, checked: fm_auth_probe/fm_auth_filter_chain/fm_auth_refuses (bin/adapters/_lib.sh:267-340), fm-worker.sh, fm-review.sh:1006, bin/lib/fm-spec-preflight.sh:87 (the spec-preflight chain filter), fm-doctor.sh:344-353, fm-setup.sh:62 read only the status word and the en/tw lines, so none changes. tests/lib/worker.sh:59, tests/lib/review.sh:30/64, tests/spec-preflight-launcher.test.sh:13 and tests/codex-review-integration.test.sh:44 copy or stub the whole probe and are unaffected. README.md:181 and skills/firstmate/SKILL.md:67 do not name the cursor command and stay.

Design, in its home section §13.3 'Setup, doctor and the vendor probe (T-121)' (design.md:4268), amended in place, no new section at the end of the file: the status-check list (about :4350) names `cursor-agent --list-models` and why; the T-188 paragraph (about :4382-4398) says the confined check is `--list-models` and gives the new cursor classification order and the three reasons; the floor list (about :4316) says cursor-agent 2026.10.01 and the 2026-10-05 recording; the Evidence paragraph (about :4557-4575) replaces 'So `cursor-agent status` does read `CURSOR_API_KEY`' with the 2026-10-05 finding that `status` ignores the key and `--list-models` reads it.

Migration and work in flight. No state, schema or event changes. Old `vendor_unavailable` events stay as records (T-188 rule; tests/worker-auth.test.sh:58-69 already covers it). The probe runs only before a round starts (bin/fm-worker.sh:1393, bin/fm-review.sh:1006, bin/lib/fm-spec-preflight.sh:87) and its result is not stored for later rounds (stale auth notes are replaced, tests/auth-probe.test.sh:164-174), so this change carries nothing over into or out of a running round and needs no in-flight handling. No task in flight touches bin/fm-auth-probe.sh.
